How to use the desk

This is a first-pass filter for player-bookings markets. It does not pick players. It tells you which fixtures and which teams carry the most card risk, so your per-fixture research starts in the right place.

Tiers, off cards against

  • Target, 2.0 cards against per game and above.
  • Mid, 1.5 to 1.9.
  • Fade, 1.4 and below.
  • Combustible (flame), 2.0 plus cards against and 12.5 plus fouls made. High cards and high fouls together.

Matchup heat

The heat score is transparent on purpose. For a fixture it is:

heat = (avgCards / 3.1 × 6) + (avgFouls / 15.4 × 4), clamped 0 to 10

avgCards is the two-team average of cards against. avgFouls is the two-team average of fouls made. Cards are weighted 60 per cent, fouls 40 per cent. The divisors 3.1 and 15.4 are the highest cards-against and fouls-made in the field, so the score is normalised against the most extreme side in the tournament.

Goalscorer markets

The Goals tab is the scoring counterpart to Matchups. Pick a fixture and it shows a goal climate, the two teams averaged over 2.5 and both-teams-score rates, plus an expected-goals readout:

exp goals = (A goals for + B goals against) / 2 + (B goals for + A goals against) / 2

Below that, each team's goal threats are ranked by a threat score, goals per 90 and expected goals per 90 weighted 60 to 40, with shots on target per 90 shown alongside. Same club form and international toggle as the bookings layer. It points you at the likely scorers, it does not price the market.

The Scorers tab is a Golden Boot board across the whole field, with three views, top threats for the tournament, top scorer for each team, and top scorer for each group. It ranks by the same threat score with low-sample players removed, and shows season goals for context. It is a rate proxy, it does not model how far a team progresses or penalties.

Where the numbers come from

Team rates are per-game figures from ScoutingStats country form, one card per team, covering all internationals. The per-fixture player layer has a club form and international toggle, both from ScoutingStats. Club form, the 2025-26 club season with broad league coverage, ranks every squad player by a risk score, yellow rate per 90 weighted double plus fouls per 90. International ranks the same way on national-team form for 2026, with hosts Mexico, USA and Canada excluded since they played no qualifiers. Each team also shows its qualifying-campaign card leaders. None of the player data feeds the tiers or heat. Referee figures are blended estimates with varying sample sizes. A confirmed-starter and referee blend layers on once line-ups and appointments are known.

Known limits

  • All 48 teams now carry form data. Sample sizes vary by team, from 12 games to 30. Smaller samples are noisier.
  • Cesar Ramos cannot referee Mexico on nationality. The watchlist notes this.
  • Referee per-game rates from short tournament samples will read high. Treat them as direction, not precision.

Your targets, notes and logged picks are saved in this browser only, under the key wc26_desk_v2. Clearing site data will remove them.

WC26 Bookings Desk. Team form via ScoutingStats. Built for research, not a betting guarantee. Stake responsibly.

Why this team works

Spine logic

  • Spain x3 (max): Two huge R1+R2 mismatches (Cabo Verde, Saudi Arabia). Yamal, Laporte, Oyarzabal cover attack and defence in one nation.
  • Germany x2: R1 v Curacao is the biggest gap of round 1 (72). Kimmich and Musiala cover both ends.
  • Belgium x2: Easiest overall group on paper (Egypt, Iran, New Zealand). De Bruyne is creative engine, Trossard the differential.
  • Switzerland x2: Cheap Group B clean sheet stack. Qatar (R1) and Bosnia (R2) both winnable.

Round by round projection

  • Round 1: Spain (Yamal, Oyarzabal, Laporte) and Germany (Kimmich, Musiala) feast on Cabo Verde and Curacao. Captain Oyarzabal for pens.
  • Round 2: Spain still strong v Saudi Arabia, Portugal v Uzbekistan, England v Ghana (Kane). Switch captain to Kane.
  • Round 3: Activate Wildcard to load up on Belgium v New Zealand (gap 76), Morocco v Haiti (75), Croatia v Ghana (63). All-new attack focus.

Honourable mentions not in the squad

Considered but cut for budget or balance: Vinicius Jr ($10m, third Brazil slot would force a $4m midfielder), Mbappe ($10.5m, France have tougher group), Haaland ($10.5m, Norway face Senegal R3), Ronaldo ($10m, age and rotation risk), Pedri ($8.1m, would break Spain max).

Transfer plan for group stages

Before R2 (2 free transfers)

Before R3 (WILDCARD)

  • Unlimited changes. Build around the R3 heavy mismatches.
  • Must-haves: Belgium attack (De Bruyne, Doku, Trossard, Lukaku), Morocco attack (Ziyech, En-Nesyri)
  • Drop: Anyone facing a tough R3 fixture (Spain v Uruguay, England v Panama)

How the model works

Assumptions and methodology

Base expected points by position and fixture tier

PositionTier 1 (60+)Tier 2 (40-59)Tier 3 (20-39)Tier 4 (under 20)
Premium FWD/MID ($8m+)9.07.55.54.0
Mid FWD/MID ($6-8m)7.05.54.53.5
Budget MID ($4-6m)5.04.03.53.0
Premium DEF ($5m+)7.05.54.03.0
Budget DEF (under $5m)5.54.53.52.5
GK6.55.54.03.0

Captain doubles base xPts. Numbers reflect goal involvement probability scaled by ranking gap, plus clean sheet odds for defensive positions. The model is intentionally conservative. Standout performances (hat tricks, 10 plus point hauls) sit outside the median.

What the model does not capture

  • Injuries and rotation
  • Red cards or penalty misses
  • Hat tricks or 3 goal hauls (these pull the average up but are not predictable)
  • Scouting bonus (under 5% ownership scoring 4+) and direct free kick bonus
  • Live form going into the tournament

FIFA World Cup 2026 Fantasy rules

Quick reference. Deadline for round 1: 20:00 UK time, Thursday 11 June 2026.

Squad

  • 15 players: 2 GK, 5 DEF, 5 MID, 3 FWD
  • Budget $100m group stage, rising to $105m from Round of 32 onwards
  • Player prices stay fixed all tournament, no price changes

Formations

4-4-2, 4-3-3, 4-5-1, 3-4-3, 3-5-2, 5-4-1, 5-3-2

Extra transfers cost minus 3 points each. Only 1 transfer can roll over to the next round, and only in the group stage.

Captain

  • Captain scores double points
  • Vice captain takes the armband only if your captain plays zero minutes and you have not changed the team during the round
  • You can change captain manually until that player's match starts

Scoring highlights

  • Each position gets 1 more point per goal vs FPL
  • Clean sheet 5 points for GK and DEF (60 mins minimum)
  • Mid +1 per 3 tackles or per 2 chances created
  • Forwards +1 per 2 shots on target
  • No defensive contribution rewards (no DefCon)
  • Penalty involvement penalises miss or save regardless of outcome
  • Bonus: 1 extra point for direct free-kick goal
  • Differential bonus: 2 points if scoring 4+ and owned by under 5% of teams

Booster planner

5 boosters across 8 rounds, only one per round. Track your plan and tick off when used.

Recommended booster plan

The strategy in one line

Save chips for moments when value is highest. Round 2 or 3 in groups, plus the knockouts. Avoid burning chips in round 1 unless you spot a clear edge.

Round 1: hold all chips

Use your unlimited pre-tournament transfers to nail your squad. Save Max Captain and 12th Man for later when fixtures sharpen.

Round 2: 12th Man on a Brazil player

Brazil v Haiti (gap 77) is the biggest mismatch of round 2. 12th Man lets Vinicius Jr count without taking a squad slot or budget. Strong shout if your squad lacks Brazilian flair.

Alternative: 12th Man on Harry Kane for England v Ghana (gap 70) if you already have Brazil exposure.

Round 3: Wildcard for full rebuild

Round 3 is when fixtures rotate hardest. Many round 1 and 2 favourites face their toughest game, and the heaviest gaps shift to Belgium v New Zealand (76), Morocco v Haiti (75), Croatia v Ghana (63), Argentina v Jordan (60).

Wildcard here lets you reload around these fixtures without taking transfer hits.

Round of 32: hold

Unlimited free transfers anyway. No need for chips. Save Qualification Booster for a round where most of your XI will progress.

Round of 16: Max Captain on a top scorer

By R16 the elite teams face stronger opposition. Max Captain guarantees your highest scorer gets the armband. Use when you have multiple strong captain options and cannot decide.

QF or SF: Qualification Booster

Use when your XI is loaded with players from teams you expect to progress. Each progressor gives +2 points. Strongest when you have 8+ likely progressors in your starting XI.

Mystery Booster: reactive

Revealed before R32. Hold and decide based on what it does.

📋 Your fantasy plan — MD1 review · MD2 · MD3

Round 1 score: 78 pts — a strong return. Squad (3-4-3): Kobel; Laporte, Kimmich, Muñoz; Raphinha, Valverde, Bruno (C), Wirtz; Kane, Oyarzabal (VC), Messi. Bench: Crépeau, Coufal, Tagliafico, Mac Allister.

What MD1 taught us

  • Captaincy was the one miss. Armband on Bruno Fernandes returned 6 (3×2); Messi hauled 19 uncaptained. Captaining Messi would have added ~13 pts. The vice (Oyarzabal, 2) was also low-ceiling — set both C and VC to genuine explosive premiums.
  • Points left on the bench: Mac Allister (8) sat while two starters blanked. Bench order/priority matters.
  • Don't overreact to one-game blanks: Raphinha (2), Valverde (2), Oyarzabal (2) all scored low but have excellent MD2 fixtures — they are holds, not sells.
  • MD1 hauls: Messi 19, Kane 13, Laporte 9, Muñoz 9, Kimmich 8 — the spine is working.

Transfers — go minimal (roll if unsure)

  • No starter has a bad fixture, so there's no forced move. Banking a free transfer toward the R3 Wildcard is defensible.
  • If you do use one: the only XI spot facing a tougher draw is the double Germany (Kimmich + Wirtz v Côte d'Ivoire). Swapping Wirtz → a Brazil / Spain / England attacker (Haiti, Saudi, Ghana fixtures) is the highest-upside single move.
  • Check Tagliafico: he didn't feature in MD1 (0). If he's not nailed-on for the Argentina XI, a free transfer to a playing defender with MD2 clean-sheet upside (Spain v Saudi, England v Ghana) is sensible — and lifts your bench cover.
  • Keep within the 3-per-nation cap (you already run 3 Argentines and 2 each of Spain/Germany).

Captaincy & bench (the real points lever)

  • Captain: Kane (v Ghana) — softest of the elite mismatches and a penalty taker. Vice: Messi — keeps the in-form explosive option as backup.
  • Differential captain: Raphinha (v Haiti) if you want to climb mini-leagues; or simply Messi (C) if you trust the MD1 form to continue.
  • Move the armband off Bruno Fernandes — good player, lower ceiling than Kane/Messi/Raphinha this round.
  • Bench priority: Mac Allister #1 (Argentina play, real start chance), then Coufal (Czechia v South Africa) over Tagliafico if his start is in doubt.

Difficulty rated on FIFA-ranking gap from the favourite's view. This is a planning aid — confirm line-ups and fitness before the round 2 deadline.

Round 3 captaincy & transfers

  • Captain Kane (England v Panama) — eliminated opponent, England must secure top spot; biggest, safest mismatch of your options.
  • Do NOT captain Messi this round — Argentina are through and top with a dead rubber v Jordan; Scaloni is likely to rest him or cap his minutes. Same caution on Mac Allister/Tagliafico and the Germany pair.
  • Vice-captain: Raphinha (Brazil v Scotland) or Valverde (Uruguay must win).
  • Transfers / Wildcard: if this is your Wildcard round, rebuild toward must-win and mismatch sides — England attack v Panama, Brazil v Scotland, Uruguay v Spain, plus clean-sheet picks from sides that need the win. Move off the Argentina/Germany rotation risks for players nailed to start.
  • Bench order: demote the Argentina assets' priority where you can — a benched Mac Allister/Tagliafico who doesn't start won't auto-sub usefully.

Transfer planner

Only 2 free transfers between rounds in the group stage. Plan carefully. Log who you want to bring in, who goes out, and the rationale.

Based on round 2 mismatches. Use these as starting points and adjust based on round 1 returns.

Captain log

Track who you captained each matchday, points scored and your reasoning. Useful for reviewing later and learning what worked.

Captain rotation plan

Round 1 captain options

Top pick: Lamine Yamal (Spain v Cabo Verde, gap 67) or Florian Wirtz (Germany v Curacao, gap 72). Both heavy mismatch favourites.

Alternatives: Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal v DR Congo, gap 41), Lionel Messi (Argentina v Algeria, gap 26).

Avoid captaining: Anyone in France v Senegal, Brazil v Morocco or England v Croatia. Too tight.

Round 2 captain options

Top pick: Vinicius Junior or Rodrygo (Brazil v Haiti, gap 77). Biggest mismatch of round 2.

Alternatives: Harry Kane (England v Ghana, gap 70), Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal v Uzbekistan, gap 45).

Round 3 captain options

Top picks: Kevin De Bruyne or Jeremy Doku (Belgium v New Zealand, gap 76), Hakim Ziyech or En-Nesyri (Morocco v Haiti, gap 75).

Alternatives: Luka Modric or Andrej Kramaric (Croatia v Ghana, gap 63), Lionel Messi (Argentina v Jordan, gap 60).

Defence stacking plan

Pick goalkeepers and defenders from teams facing the biggest ranking gap underdogs. Clean sheets pay 5 points to GK and DEF if 60+ minutes played.

Squad spine recommendation

Teams with the most lopsided fixtures across the group stage. Per-nation max is 3, so pick 2-3 players from these nations.
